artists.biography:
Amplifier are a progressive rock band from Manchester, England. The band has released four albums and two EPs since its inception in 1999. Their self-titled debut album was released in 2004 by Music for Nations. Their second album, Insider was released in Europe in 2006 on the SPV label. Their third album, The Octopus, was released to fans in December 2010 ahead of a full release in January 2011. The band's fourth album, Echo Street, was released in March 2013.

Amplifier's sound has been described as "Soundgarden, Tool, Black Sabbath, Oceansize and Pink Floyd taking copious amounts of mind-altering substances and venturing on a trip through time and space (to another dimension), and back again." Their music is characterised by lead singer and guitarist Balamir's effects pedals, extended heavy sections, atmospheric compositions and philosophical lyrics mainly dealing with astronomy, the cosmos and the darker side of human nature.

perplexity.description:
Residue is a 2014 EP by the British rock band Amplifier, released during a period of transition as the band moved to the Superball Music label. Musically, Residue continues Amplifier’s signature blend of alternative rock, space rock, and progressive elements, characterized by atmospheric guitar textures, introspective lyrics, and dynamic song structures. The EP showcases the band’s ability to merge melodic sensibilities with expansive sonic landscapes, reflecting their ongoing evolution within the rock genre.

Within Amplifier’s discography, Residue serves as a companion piece to their fifth studio album, Mystoria, featuring outtakes and additional material from those sessions. It was followed by Residue Part 2 in 2015, further expanding on the themes and sounds explored during this era. While not a full-length album, Residue was well-received by fans and critics for its consistency and depth, reinforcing Amplifier’s reputation for crafting thoughtful, genre-blurring rock music. The original release in 2014 helped solidify the band’s presence in the progressive and alternative rock scenes, leading to continued support and recognition in subsequent years.
